./CHANGELOG.md:394:13.0.0 (2021-06-12)
./CHANGELOG.md:395:===================
./CHANGELOG.md:396:ripgrep 13 is a new major version release of ripgrep that primarily contains
./CHANGELOG.md:397:bug fixes, some performance improvements and a few minor breaking changes.
./CHANGELOG.md:398:There is also a fix for a security vulnerability on Windows
./CHANGELOG.md:399:([CVE-2021-3013](https://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2021-3013)).
./CHANGELOG.md:400:
./CHANGELOG.md:401:Some highlights:
./CHANGELOG.md:402:
./CHANGELOG.md:403:A new short flag, `-.`, has been added. It is an alias for the `--hidden` flag,
./CHANGELOG.md:404:which instructs ripgrep to search hidden files and directories.
./CHANGELOG.md:405:
./CHANGELOG.md:406:ripgrep is now using a new
./CHANGELOG.md:407:[vectorized implementation of `memmem`](https://github.com/BurntSushi/memchr/pull/82),
./CHANGELOG.md:408:which accelerates many common searches. If you notice any performance
./CHANGELOG.md:409:regressions (or major improvements), I'd love to hear about them through an
./CHANGELOG.md:410:issue report!
./CHANGELOG.md:411:
./CHANGELOG.md:412:Also, for Windows users targeting MSVC, Cargo will now build fully static
./CHANGELOG.md:413:executables of ripgrep. The release binaries for ripgrep 13 have been compiled
./CHANGELOG.md:414:using this configuration.
./CHANGELOG.md:415:
./CHANGELOG.md:416:**BREAKING CHANGES**:
./CHANGELOG.md:417:
./CHANGELOG.md:418:**Binary detection output has changed slightly.**
./CHANGELOG.md:419:
./CHANGELOG.md:420:In this release, a small tweak has been made to the output format when a binary
./CHANGELOG.md:421:file is detected. Previously, it looked like this:
./CHANGELOG.md:422:
./CHANGELOG.md:423:```
./CHANGELOG.md:424:Binary file FOO matches (found "\0" byte around offset XXX)
./CHANGELOG.md:425:```
./CHANGELOG.md:426:
./CHANGELOG.md:427:Now it looks like this:
./CHANGELOG.md:428:
./CHANGELOG.md:429:```
./CHANGELOG.md:430:FOO: binary file matches (found "\0" byte around offset XXX)
./CHANGELOG.md:431:```
./CHANGELOG.md:432:
./CHANGELOG.md:433:**vimgrep output in multi-line now only prints the first line for each match.**
./CHANGELOG.md:434:
./CHANGELOG.md:435:See [issue 1866](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/issues/1866) for more
./CHANGELOG.md:436:discussion on this. Previously, every line in a match was duplicated, even
./CHANGELOG.md:437:when it spanned multiple lines. There are no changes to vimgrep output when
./CHANGELOG.md:438:multi-line mode is disabled.
./CHANGELOG.md:439:
./CHANGELOG.md:440:**In multi-line mode, --count is now equivalent to --count-matches.**
./CHANGELOG.md:441:
./CHANGELOG.md:442:This appears to match how `pcre2grep` implements `--count`. Previously, ripgrep
./CHANGELOG.md:443:would produce outright incorrect counts. Another alternative would be to simply
./CHANGELOG.md:444:count the number of lines---even if it's more than the number of matches---but
./CHANGELOG.md:445:that seems highly unintuitive.
./CHANGELOG.md:446:
./CHANGELOG.md:447:**FULL LIST OF FIXES AND IMPROVEMENTS:**
./CHANGELOG.md:448:
./CHANGELOG.md:449:Security fixes:
./CHANGELOG.md:450:
./CHANGELOG.md:451:* [CVE-2021-3013](https://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2021-3013):
./CHANGELOG.md:452:  Fixes a security hole on Windows where running ripgrep with either the
./CHANGELOG.md:453:  `-z/--search-zip` or `--pre` flags can result in running arbitrary
./CHANGELOG.md:454:  executables from the current directory.
./CHANGELOG.md:455:* [VULN #1773](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/issues/1773):
./CHANGELOG.md:456:  This is the public facing issue tracking CVE-2021-3013. ripgrep's README
./CHANGELOG.md:457:  now contains a section describing how to report a vulnerability.

./CHANGELOG.md:531:ripgrep 12.1.1 is a patch release that fixes a couple small bugs. In
./CHANGELOG.md:532:particular, the ripgrep 12.1.0 release did not tag new releases for all of its
./CHANGELOG.md:533:in-tree dependencies. As a result, ripgrep built dependencies from crates.io
./CHANGELOG.md:534:would produce a different build than compiling ripgrep from source on the
./CHANGELOG.md:535:`12.1.0` tag. Namely, some crates like `grep-cli` had unreleased changes.

./CHANGELOG.md:551:notices for downstream packagers.

./CHANGELOG.md:556:  See [#1577](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/issues/1577)
./CHANGELOG.md:557:  for more details.

./CHANGELOG.md:560:  `a2x`. Support for `a2x` will be dropped in the ripgrep 13 release.

./CHANGELOG.md:728:11.0.0 (2019-04-15)
./CHANGELOG.md:729:===================
./CHANGELOG.md:730:ripgrep 11 is a new major version release of ripgrep that contains many bug
./CHANGELOG.md:731:fixes, some performance improvements and a few feature enhancements. Notably,
./CHANGELOG.md:732:ripgrep's user experience for binary file filtering has been improved. See the
./CHANGELOG.md:733:[guide's new section on binary data](GUIDE.md#binary-data) for more details.
./CHANGELOG.md:734:
./CHANGELOG.md:735:This release also marks a change in ripgrep's versioning. Where as the previous
./CHANGELOG.md:736:version was `0.10.0`, this version is `11.0.0`. Moving forward, ripgrep's
./CHANGELOG.md:737:major version will be increased a few times per year. ripgrep will continue to
./CHANGELOG.md:738:be conservative with respect to backwards compatibility, but may occasionally
./CHANGELOG.md:739:introduce breaking changes, which will always be documented in this CHANGELOG.
./CHANGELOG.md:740:See [issue 1172](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/issues/1172) for a bit
./CHANGELOG.md:741:more detail on why this versioning change was made.
./CHANGELOG.md:742:
./CHANGELOG.md:743:This release increases the **minimum supported Rust version** from 1.28.0 to
./CHANGELOG.md:744:1.34.0.
./CHANGELOG.md:745:
./CHANGELOG.md:746:**BREAKING CHANGES**:
./CHANGELOG.md:747:
./CHANGELOG.md:748:* ripgrep has tweaked its exit status codes to be more like GNU grep's. Namely,
./CHANGELOG.md:749:  if a non-fatal error occurs during a search, then ripgrep will now always
./CHANGELOG.md:750:  emit a `2` exit status code, regardless of whether a match is found or not.
./CHANGELOG.md:751:  Previously, ripgrep would only emit a `2` exit status code for a catastrophic
./CHANGELOG.md:752:  error (e.g., regex syntax error). One exception to this is if ripgrep is run
./CHANGELOG.md:753:  with `-q/--quiet`. In that case, if an error occurs and a match is found,
./CHANGELOG.md:754:  then ripgrep will exit with a `0` exit status code.
./CHANGELOG.md:755:* Supplying the `-u/--unrestricted` flag three times is now equivalent to
./CHANGELOG.md:756:  supplying `--no-ignore --hidden --binary`. Previously, `-uuu` was equivalent
./CHANGELOG.md:757:  to `--no-ignore --hidden --text`. The difference is that `--binary` disables
./CHANGELOG.md:758:  binary file filtering without potentially dumping binary data into your
./CHANGELOG.md:759:  terminal. That is, `rg -uuu foo` should now be equivalent to `grep -r foo`.
./CHANGELOG.md:760:* The `avx-accel` feature of ripgrep has been removed since it is no longer
./CHANGELOG.md:761:  necessary. All uses of AVX in ripgrep are now enabled automatically via
./CHANGELOG.md:762:  runtime CPU feature detection. The `simd-accel` feature does remain available
./CHANGELOG.md:763:  (only for enabling SIMD for transcoding), however, it does increase
./CHANGELOG.md:764:  compilation times substantially at the moment.

./CHANGELOG.md:856:0.10.0 (2018-09-07)
./CHANGELOG.md:857:===================
./CHANGELOG.md:858:This is a new minor version release of ripgrep that contains some major new
./CHANGELOG.md:859:features, a huge number of bug fixes, and is the first release based on
./CHANGELOG.md:860:libripgrep. The entirety of ripgrep's core search and printing code has been

./CHANGELOG.md:862:

./CHANGELOG.md:864:format.
./CHANGELOG.md:865:
./CHANGELOG.md:866:**BREAKING CHANGES**:
./CHANGELOG.md:867:
./CHANGELOG.md:868:* The minimum version required to compile Rust has now changed to track the
./CHANGELOG.md:869:  latest stable version of Rust. Patch releases will continue to compile with
./CHANGELOG.md:870:  the same version of Rust as the previous patch release, but new minor
./CHANGELOG.md:871:  versions will use the current stable version of the Rust compile as its
./CHANGELOG.md:872:  minimum supported version.
./CHANGELOG.md:873:* The match semantics of `-w/--word-regexp` have changed slightly. They used
./CHANGELOG.md:874:  to be `\b(?:<your pattern>)\b`, but now it's
./CHANGELOG.md:875:  `(?:^|\W)(?:<your pattern>)(?:$|\W)`. This matches the behavior of GNU grep
./CHANGELOG.md:876:  and is believed to be closer to the intended semantics of the flag. See
./CHANGELOG.md:877:  [#389](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/issues/389) for more details.

./CHANGELOG.md:941:0.9.0 (2018-08-03)
./CHANGELOG.md:942:==================
./CHANGELOG.md:943:This is a new minor version release of ripgrep that contains some minor new
./CHANGELOG.md:944:features and a panoply of bug fixes.
./CHANGELOG.md:945:
./CHANGELOG.md:946:Releases provided on Github for `x86_64` will now work on all target CPUs, and
./CHANGELOG.md:947:will also automatically take advantage of features found on modern CPUs (such
./CHANGELOG.md:948:as AVX2) for additional optimizations.
./CHANGELOG.md:949:
./CHANGELOG.md:950:This release increases the **minimum supported Rust version** from 1.20.0 to
./CHANGELOG.md:951:1.23.0.
./CHANGELOG.md:952:
./CHANGELOG.md:953:It is anticipated that the next release of ripgrep (0.10.0) will provide
./CHANGELOG.md:954:multi-line search support and a JSON output format.
./CHANGELOG.md:955:
./CHANGELOG.md:956:**BREAKING CHANGES**:
./CHANGELOG.md:957:
./CHANGELOG.md:958:* When `--count` and `--only-matching` are provided simultaneously, the
./CHANGELOG.md:959:  behavior of ripgrep is as if the `--count-matches` flag was given. That is,
./CHANGELOG.md:960:  the total number of matches is reported, where there may be multiple matches
./CHANGELOG.md:961:  per line. Previously, the behavior of ripgrep was to report the total number
./CHANGELOG.md:962:  of matching lines. (Note that this behavior diverges from the behavior of
./CHANGELOG.md:963:  GNU grep.)
./CHANGELOG.md:964:* Octal syntax is no longer supported. ripgrep previously accepted expressions
./CHANGELOG.md:965:  like `\1` as syntax for matching `U+0001`, but ripgrep will now report an
./CHANGELOG.md:966:  error instead.
./CHANGELOG.md:967:* The `--line-number-width` flag has been removed. Its functionality was not
./CHANGELOG.md:968:  carefully considered with all ripgrep output formats.
./CHANGELOG.md:969:  See [#795](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/issues/795) for more
./CHANGELOG.md:970:  details.

./CHANGELOG.md:1096:0.8.0 (2018-02-11)
./CHANGELOG.md:1097:==================
./CHANGELOG.md:1098:This is a new minor version release of ripgrep that satisfies several popular
./CHANGELOG.md:1099:feature requests (config files, search compressed files, true colors), fixes
./CHANGELOG.md:1100:many bugs and improves the quality of life for ripgrep maintainers. This
./CHANGELOG.md:1101:release also includes greatly improved documentation in the form of a
./CHANGELOG.md:1102:[User Guide](GUIDE.md) and a [FAQ](FAQ.md).
./CHANGELOG.md:1103:
./CHANGELOG.md:1104:This release increases the **minimum supported Rust version** from 1.17 to
./CHANGELOG.md:1105:1.20.
./CHANGELOG.md:1106:
./CHANGELOG.md:1107:**BREAKING CHANGES**:
./CHANGELOG.md:1108:
./CHANGELOG.md:1109:Note that these are all very minor and unlikely to impact most users.
./CHANGELOG.md:1110:
./CHANGELOG.md:1111:* In order to support configuration files, flag overrides needed to be
./CHANGELOG.md:1112:  rethought. In some cases, this changed ripgrep's behavior. For example,
./CHANGELOG.md:1113:  in ripgrep 0.7.1, `rg foo -s -i` will perform a case sensitive search
./CHANGELOG.md:1114:  since the `-s/--case-sensitive` flag was defined to always take precedence
./CHANGELOG.md:1115:  over the `-i/--ignore-case` flag, regardless of position. In ripgrep 0.8.0
./CHANGELOG.md:1116:  however, the override rule for all flags has changed to "the most recent
./CHANGELOG.md:1117:  flag wins among competing flags." That is, `rg foo -s -i` now performs a
./CHANGELOG.md:1118:  case insensitive search.
./CHANGELOG.md:1119:* The `-M/--max-columns` flag was tweaked so that specifying a value of `0`
./CHANGELOG.md:1120:  now makes ripgrep behave as if the flag was absent. This makes it possible
./CHANGELOG.md:1121:  to set a default value in a configuration file and then override it. The
./CHANGELOG.md:1122:  previous ripgrep behavior was to suppress all matching non-empty lines.
./CHANGELOG.md:1123:* In all globs, `[^...]` is now equivalent to `[!...]` (indicating class
./CHANGELOG.md:1124:  negation). Previously, `^` had no special significance in a character class.
./CHANGELOG.md:1125:* For **downstream packagers**, the directory hierarchy in ripgrep's archive
./CHANGELOG.md:1126:  releases has changed. The root directory now only contains the executable,
./CHANGELOG.md:1127:  README and license. There is now a new directory called `doc` which contains
./CHANGELOG.md:1128:  the man page (previously in the root), a user guide (new), a FAQ (new) and
./CHANGELOG.md:1129:  the CHANGELOG (previously not included in release). The `complete`
./CHANGELOG.md:1130:  directory remains the same.
./CHANGELOG.md:1131:
./CHANGELOG.md:1132:Feature enhancements:
./CHANGELOG.md:1133:
./CHANGELOG.md:1134:* Added or improved file type filtering for
./CHANGELOG.md:1135:  Apache Avro, C++, GN, Google Closure Templates, Jupyter notebooks, man pages,
./CHANGELOG.md:1136:  Protocol Buffers, Smarty and Web IDL.
./CHANGELOG.md:1137:* [FEATURE #196](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/issues/196):
./CHANGELOG.md:1138:  Support a configuration file. See
./CHANGELOG.md:1139:  [the new user guide](GUIDE.md#configuration-file)
./CHANGELOG.md:1140:  for details.
./CHANGELOG.md:1141:* [FEATURE #261](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/issues/261):
./CHANGELOG.md:1142:  Add extended or "true" color support. Works in Windows 10!
./CHANGELOG.md:1143:  [See the FAQ for details.](FAQ.md#colors)
./CHANGELOG.md:1144:* [FEATURE #539](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/issues/539):
./CHANGELOG.md:1145:  Search gzip, bzip2, lzma or xz files when given `-z/--search-zip` flag.
./CHANGELOG.md:1146:* [FEATURE #544](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/issues/544):
./CHANGELOG.md:1147:  Add support for line number alignment via a new `--line-number-width` flag.
./CHANGELOG.md:1148:* [FEATURE #654](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/pull/654):
./CHANGELOG.md:1149:  Support linuxbrew in ripgrep's Brew tap.
./CHANGELOG.md:1150:* [FEATURE #673](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/issues/673):
./CHANGELOG.md:1151:  Bring back `.rgignore` files. (A higher precedent, application specific

./CHANGELOG.md:1384:0.5.0 (2017-03-12)
./CHANGELOG.md:1385:==================
./CHANGELOG.md:1386:This is a new minor version release of ripgrep that includes one minor breaking
./CHANGELOG.md:1387:change, bug fixes and several new features including support for text encodings
./CHANGELOG.md:1388:other than UTF-8.
./CHANGELOG.md:1389:
./CHANGELOG.md:1390:A notable accomplishment with respect to Rust is that ripgrep proper now only
./CHANGELOG.md:1391:contains a single `unsafe` use (for accessing the contents of a memory map).
./CHANGELOG.md:1392:
./CHANGELOG.md:1393:The **breaking change** is:
./CHANGELOG.md:1394:
./CHANGELOG.md:1395:* [FEATURE #380](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/issues/380):
./CHANGELOG.md:1396:  Line numbers are now hidden by default when ripgrep is printing to a tty
./CHANGELOG.md:1397:  **and** the only thing searched is stdin.
./CHANGELOG.md:1398:
./CHANGELOG.md:1399:Feature enhancements:
./CHANGELOG.md:1400:
./CHANGELOG.md:1401:* Added or improved file type filtering for Ceylon, CSS, Elixir, HTML, log,
./CHANGELOG.md:1402:  SASS, SVG, Twig
./CHANGELOG.md:1403:* [FEATURE #1](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/issues/1):
./CHANGELOG.md:1404:  Add support for additional text encodings, including automatic detection for
./CHANGELOG.md:1405:  UTF-16 via BOM sniffing. Explicit text encoding support with the
./CHANGELOG.md:1406:  `-E/--encoding` flag was also added for latin-1, GBK, EUC-JP
./CHANGELOG.md:1407:  and Shift_JIS, among others. The full list can be found here:
./CHANGELOG.md:1408:  https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-encoding-get
./CHANGELOG.md:1409:* [FEATURE #129](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/issues/129):
./CHANGELOG.md:1410:  Add a new `-M/--max-columns` flag that omits lines longer than the given
./CHANGELOG.md:1411:  number of bytes. (Disabled by default!)
./CHANGELOG.md:1412:* [FEATURE #369](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/issues/369):
./CHANGELOG.md:1413:  A new flag, `--max-filesize`, was added for limiting searches to files with
./CHANGELOG.md:1414:  a maximum file size.
./CHANGELOG.md:1415:
./CHANGELOG.md:1416:Bug fixes:
./CHANGELOG.md:1417:
./CHANGELOG.md:1418:* [BUG #52](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/issues/52),
./CHANGELOG.md:1419:  [BUG #311](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/issues/311):
./CHANGELOG.md:1420:  Tweak how binary files are detected and handled. (We are slightly less
./CHANGELOG.md:1421:  conservative and will no longer use memory without bound.)
./CHANGELOG.md:1422:* [BUG #326](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/issues/326):
./CHANGELOG.md:1423:  When --files flag is given, we should never attempt to parse positional
./CHANGELOG.md:1424:  arguments as regexes.
./CHANGELOG.md:1425:* [BUG #327](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/issues/327):
./CHANGELOG.md:1426:  Permit the --heading flag to override the --no-heading flag.
./CHANGELOG.md:1427:* [BUG #340](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/pull/340):
./CHANGELOG.md:1428:  Clarify that the `-u/--unrestricted` flags are aliases.

./CHANGELOG.md:1447:=====
./CHANGELOG.md:1448:This is a new minor version release of ripgrep that includes a couple very
./CHANGELOG.md:1449:minor breaking changes, a few new features and lots of bug fixes.
./CHANGELOG.md:1450:
./CHANGELOG.md:1451:This version of ripgrep upgrades its `regex` dependency from `0.1` to `0.2`,
./CHANGELOG.md:1452:which includes a few minor syntax changes:
./CHANGELOG.md:1453:
./CHANGELOG.md:1454:* POSIX character classes now require double bracketing. Previously, the regex
./CHANGELOG.md:1455:  `[:upper:]` would parse as the `upper` POSIX character class. Now it parses
./CHANGELOG.md:1456:  as the character class containing the characters `:upper:`. The fix to this
./CHANGELOG.md:1457:  change is to use `[[:upper:]]` instead. Note that variants like
./CHANGELOG.md:1458:  `[[:upper:][:blank:]]` continue to work.
./CHANGELOG.md:1459:* The character `[` must always be escaped inside a character class.
./CHANGELOG.md:1460:* The characters `&`, `-` and `~` must be escaped if any one of them are
./CHANGELOG.md:1461:  repeated consecutively. For example, `[&]`, `[\&]`, `[\&\&]`, `[&-&]` are all
./CHANGELOG.md:1462:  equivalent while `[&&]` is illegal. (The motivation for this and the prior
./CHANGELOG.md:1463:  change is to provide a backwards compatible path for adding character class
./CHANGELOG.md:1464:  set notation.)

./CHANGELOG.md:1550:=====
./CHANGELOG.md:1551:This is a new minor version release of ripgrep that includes two breaking
./CHANGELOG.md:1552:changes with lots of bug fixes and some new features and performance
./CHANGELOG.md:1553:improvements. Notably, if you had a problem with colors or piping on Windows
./CHANGELOG.md:1554:before, then that should now be fixed in this release.
./CHANGELOG.md:1555:
./CHANGELOG.md:1556:**BREAKING CHANGES**:
./CHANGELOG.md:1557:
./CHANGELOG.md:1558:* ripgrep now requires Rust 1.11 to compile. Previously, it could build on
./CHANGELOG.md:1559:  Rust 1.9. The cause of this was the move from
./CHANGELOG.md:1560:  [Docopt to Clap](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/pull/233)
./CHANGELOG.md:1561:  for argument parsing.
./CHANGELOG.md:1562:* The `-e/--regexp` flag can no longer accept a pattern starting with a `-`.
./CHANGELOG.md:1563:  There are two work-arounds: `rg -- -foo` and `rg [-]foo` or `rg -e [-]foo`
./CHANGELOG.md:1564:  will all search for the same `-foo` pattern. The cause of this was the move
./CHANGELOG.md:1565:  from [Docopt to Clap](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/pull/233)
./CHANGELOG.md:1566:  for argument parsing.
./CHANGELOG.md:1567:  [This may get fixed in the
./CHANGELOG.md:1568:  future.](https://github.com/kbknapp/clap-rs/issues/742).
./CHANGELOG.md:1569:
./CHANGELOG.md:1570:Performance improvements:

./CHANGELOG.md:1572:* [PERF #33](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/issues/33):

./CHANGELOG.md:1574:* [PERF #136](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/issues/136):

./CHANGELOG.md:1774:* [FEATURE #89](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/issues/89):
./CHANGELOG.md:1775:  Add a --null flag that outputs a NUL byte after every file path.
./CHANGELOG.md:1776:
./CHANGELOG.md:1777:Bug fixes:
./CHANGELOG.md:1778:
./CHANGELOG.md:1779:* [BUG #98](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/issues/98):
./CHANGELOG.md:1780:  Fix a bug in single threaded mode when if opening a file failed, ripgrep
./CHANGELOG.md:1781:  quit instead of continuing the search.
./CHANGELOG.md:1782:* [BUG #99](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/issues/99):
./CHANGELOG.md:1783:  Fix another bug in single threaded mode where empty lines were being printed
./CHANGELOG.md:1784:  by mistake.
./CHANGELOG.md:1785:* [BUG #105](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/issues/105):
./CHANGELOG.md:1786:  Fix an off-by-one error with --column.
./CHANGELOG.md:1787:* [BUG #106](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/issues/106):
./CHANGELOG.md:1788:  Fix a bug where a whitespace only line in a gitignore file caused ripgrep

./CHANGELOG.md:1793:=====
./CHANGELOG.md:1794:Feature enhancements:
./CHANGELOG.md:1795:
./CHANGELOG.md:1796:* Added or improved file type filtering for VB, R, F#, Swift, Nim, JavaScript,
./CHANGELOG.md:1797:  TypeScript
./CHANGELOG.md:1798:* [FEATURE #20](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/issues/20):

./CHANGELOG.md:1800:* [FEATURE #26](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/issues/26):

./CHANGELOG.md:1802:  and doesn't need to count every match.
./CHANGELOG.md:1803:* [FEATURE #40](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/issues/40):
./CHANGELOG.md:1804:  Switch from using `.rgignore` to `.ignore`. Note that `.rgignore` is
./CHANGELOG.md:1805:  still supported, but deprecated.
./CHANGELOG.md:1806:* [FEATURE #68](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/issues/68):
./CHANGELOG.md:1807:  Add --no-ignore-vcs flag that ignores .gitignore but not .ignore.
./CHANGELOG.md:1808:* [FEATURE #70](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/issues/70):
./CHANGELOG.md:1809:  Add -S/--smart-case flag (but is disabled by default).
./CHANGELOG.md:1810:* [FEATURE #80](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/issues/80):
./CHANGELOG.md:1811:  Add support for `{foo,bar}` globs.
./CHANGELOG.md:1812:
./CHANGELOG.md:1813:Many many bug fixes. Thanks every for reporting these and helping make
./CHANGELOG.md:1814:`ripgrep` better! (Note that I haven't captured every tracking issue here,
./CHANGELOG.md:1815:some were closed as duplicates.)
./CHANGELOG.md:1816:
./CHANGELOG.md:1817:* [BUG #8](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/issues/8):
./CHANGELOG.md:1818:  Don't use an intermediate buffer when --threads=1. (Permits constant memory
./CHANGELOG.md:1819:  usage.)
./CHANGELOG.md:1820:* [BUG #15](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/issues/15):
./CHANGELOG.md:1821:  Improves the documentation for --type-add.
./CHANGELOG.md:1822:* [BUG #16](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/issues/16),
./CHANGELOG.md:1823:  [BUG #49](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/issues/49),
./CHANGELOG.md:1824:  [BUG #50](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/issues/50),
./CHANGELOG.md:1825:  [BUG #65](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/issues/65):
./CHANGELOG.md:1826:  Some gitignore globs were being treated as anchored when they weren't.
./CHANGELOG.md:1827:* [BUG #18](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/issues/18):
./CHANGELOG.md:1828:  --vimgrep reported incorrect column number.
./CHANGELOG.md:1829:* [BUG #19](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/issues/19):
./CHANGELOG.md:1830:  ripgrep was hanging waiting on stdin in some Windows terminals. Note that
./CHANGELOG.md:1831:  this introduced a new bug:
./CHANGELOG.md:1832:  [#94](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/issues/94).
./CHANGELOG.md:1833:* [BUG #21](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/issues/21):
./CHANGELOG.md:1834:  Removes leading `./` when printing file paths.
./CHANGELOG.md:1835:* [BUG #22](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/issues/22):
./CHANGELOG.md:1836:  Running `rg --help | echo` caused `rg` to panic.
./CHANGELOG.md:1837:* [BUG #24](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/issues/22):
./CHANGELOG.md:1838:  Clarify the central purpose of rg in its usage message.
./CHANGELOG.md:1839:* [BUG #25](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/issues/25):
./CHANGELOG.md:1840:  Anchored gitignore globs weren't applied in subdirectories correctly.
./CHANGELOG.md:1841:* [BUG #30](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/issues/30):
./CHANGELOG.md:1842:  Globs like `foo/**` should match contents of `foo`, but not `foo` itself.
./CHANGELOG.md:1843:* [BUG #35](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/issues/35),
./CHANGELOG.md:1844:  [BUG #81](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/issues/81):
./CHANGELOG.md:1845:  When automatically detecting stdin, only read if it's a file or a fifo.
./CHANGELOG.md:1846:  i.e., ignore stdin in `rg foo < /dev/null`.
./CHANGELOG.md:1847:* [BUG #36](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/issues/36):
./CHANGELOG.md:1848:  Don't automatically pick memory maps on MacOS. Ever.
./CHANGELOG.md:1849:* [BUG #38](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/issues/38):
./CHANGELOG.md:1850:  Trailing whitespace in gitignore wasn't being ignored.
./CHANGELOG.md:1851:* [BUG #43](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/issues/43):
./CHANGELOG.md:1852:  --glob didn't work with directories.
./CHANGELOG.md:1853:* [BUG #46](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/issues/46):
./CHANGELOG.md:1854:  Use one fewer worker thread than what is provided on CLI.
./CHANGELOG.md:1855:* [BUG #47](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/issues/47):
./CHANGELOG.md:1856:  --help/--version now work even if other options are set.
./CHANGELOG.md:1857:* [BUG #55](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/issues/55):
./CHANGELOG.md:1858:  ripgrep was refusing to search /proc/cpuinfo. Fixed by disabling memory
./CHANGELOG.md:1859:  maps for files with zero size.
./CHANGELOG.md:1860:* [BUG #64](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/issues/64):
./CHANGELOG.md:1861:  The first path given with --files set was ignored.
./CHANGELOG.md:1862:* [BUG #67](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/issues/67):
./CHANGELOG.md:1863:  Sometimes whitelist globs like `!/dir` weren't interpreted as anchored.
./CHANGELOG.md:1864:* [BUG #77](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/issues/77):
./CHANGELOG.md:1865:  When -q/--quiet flag was passed, ripgrep kept searching even after a match
./CHANGELOG.md:1866:  was found.
./CHANGELOG.md:1867:* [BUG #90](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/issues/90):
./CHANGELOG.md:1868:  Permit whitelisting hidden files.
./CHANGELOG.md:1869:* [BUG #93](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/issues/93):
./CHANGELOG.md:1870:  ripgrep was extracting an erroneous inner literal from a repeated pattern.

./crates/printer/src/json.rs:128:/// ## Overview
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:129:///
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:130:/// The format of this printer is the [JSON Lines](https://jsonlines.org/)
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:131:/// format. Specifically, this printer emits a sequence of messages, where
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:132:/// each message is encoded as a single JSON value on a single line. There are
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:133:/// four different types of messages (and this number may expand over time):
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:134:///
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:135:/// * **begin** - A message that indicates a file is being searched.
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:136:/// * **end** - A message the indicates a file is done being searched. This
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:137:///   message also include summary statistics about the search.
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:138:/// * **match** - A message that indicates a match was found. This includes
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:139:///   the text and offsets of the match.
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:140:/// * **context** - A message that indicates a contextual line was found.
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:141:///   This includes the text of the line, along with any match information if
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:142:///   the search was inverted.
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:143:///
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:144:/// Every message is encoded in the same envelope format, which includes a tag
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:145:/// indicating the message type along with an object for the payload:
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:146:///
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:147:/// ```json
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:148:/// {
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:149:///     "type": "{begin|end|match|context}",
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:150:///     "data": { ... }
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:151:/// }
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:152:/// ```
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:153:///
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:154:/// The message itself is encoded in the envelope's `data` key.
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:155:///
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:156:/// ## Text encoding
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:157:///
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:158:/// Before describing each message format, we first must briefly discuss text
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:159:/// encoding, since it factors into every type of message. In particular, JSON
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:160:/// may only be encoded in UTF-8, UTF-16 or UTF-32. For the purposes of this
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:161:/// printer, we need only worry about UTF-8. The problem here is that searching
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:162:/// is not limited to UTF-8 exclusively, which in turn implies that matches
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:163:/// may be reported that contain invalid UTF-8. Moreover, this printer may
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:164:/// also print file paths, and the encoding of file paths is itself not
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:165:/// guaranteed to be valid UTF-8. Therefore, this printer must deal with the
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:166:/// presence of invalid UTF-8 somehow. The printer could silently ignore such
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:167:/// things completely, or even lossily transcode invalid UTF-8 to valid UTF-8
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:168:/// by replacing all invalid sequences with the Unicode replacement character.
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:169:/// However, this would prevent consumers of this format from accessing the
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:170:/// original data in a non-lossy way.
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:171:///
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:172:/// Therefore, this printer will emit valid UTF-8 encoded bytes as normal
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:173:/// JSON strings and otherwise base64 encode data that isn't valid UTF-8. To
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:174:/// communicate whether this process occurs or not, strings are keyed by the
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:175:/// name `text` where as arbitrary bytes are keyed by `bytes`.
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:176:///
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:177:/// For example, when a path is included in a message, it is formatted like so,
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:178:/// if and only if the path is valid UTF-8:
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:179:///
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:180:/// ```json
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:181:/// {
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:182:///     "path": {
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:183:///         "text": "/home/ubuntu/lib.rs"
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:184:///     }
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:185:/// }
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:186:/// ```
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:187:///
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:188:/// If instead our path was `/home/ubuntu/lib\xFF.rs`, where the `\xFF` byte
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:189:/// makes it invalid UTF-8, the path would instead be encoded like so:
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:190:///
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:191:/// ```json
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:192:/// {
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:193:///     "path": {
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:194:///         "bytes": "L2hvbWUvdWJ1bnR1L2xpYv8ucnM="
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:195:///     }
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:196:/// }
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:197:/// ```
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:198:///
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:199:/// This same representation is used for reporting matches as well.
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:200:///
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:201:/// The printer guarantees that the `text` field is used whenever the
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:202:/// underlying bytes are valid UTF-8.
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:203:///
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:204:/// ## Wire format
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:205:///
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:206:/// This section documents the wire format emitted by this printer, starting
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:207:/// with the four types of messages.
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:208:///
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:209:/// Each message has its own format, and is contained inside an envelope that
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:210:/// indicates the type of message. The envelope has these fields:
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:211:///
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:212:/// * **type** - A string indicating the type of this message. It may be one
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:213:///   of four possible strings: `begin`, `end`, `match` or `context`. This
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:214:///   list may expand over time.
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:215:/// * **data** - The actual message data. The format of this field depends on
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:216:///   the value of `type`. The possible message formats are
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:217:///   [`begin`](#message-begin),
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:218:///   [`end`](#message-end),
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:219:///   [`match`](#message-match),
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:220:///   [`context`](#message-context).
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:221:///
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:222:/// #### Message: **begin**
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:223:///
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:224:/// This message indicates that a search has begun. It has these fields:
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:225:///
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:226:/// * **path** - An
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:227:///   [arbitrary data object](#object-arbitrary-data)
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:228:///   representing the file path corresponding to the search, if one is
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:229:///   present. If no file path is available, then this field is `null`.
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:230:///
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:231:/// #### Message: **end**
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:232:///
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:233:/// This message indicates that a search has finished. It has these fields:
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:234:///
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:235:/// * **path** - An
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:236:///   [arbitrary data object](#object-arbitrary-data)
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:237:///   representing the file path corresponding to the search, if one is
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:238:///   present. If no file path is available, then this field is `null`.
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:239:/// * **binary_offset** - The absolute offset in the data searched
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:240:///   corresponding to the place at which binary data was detected. If no
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:241:///   binary data was detected (or if binary detection was disabled), then this
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:242:///   field is `null`.
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:243:/// * **stats** - A [`stats` object](#object-stats) that contains summary
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:244:///   statistics for the previous search.
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:245:///
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:246:/// #### Message: **match**
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:247:///
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:248:/// This message indicates that a match has been found. A match generally
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:249:/// corresponds to a single line of text, although it may correspond to
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:250:/// multiple lines if the search can emit matches over multiple lines. It
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:251:/// has these fields:
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:252:///
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:253:/// * **path** - An
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:254:///   [arbitrary data object](#object-arbitrary-data)
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:255:///   representing the file path corresponding to the search, if one is
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:256:///   present. If no file path is available, then this field is `null`.
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:257:/// * **lines** - An
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:258:///   [arbitrary data object](#object-arbitrary-data)
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:259:///   representing one or more lines contained in this match.
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:260:/// * **line_number** - If the searcher has been configured to report line
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:261:///   numbers, then this corresponds to the line number of the first line
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:262:///   in `lines`. If no line numbers are available, then this is `null`.
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:263:/// * **absolute_offset** - The absolute byte offset corresponding to the start
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:264:///   of `lines` in the data being searched.
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:265:/// * **submatches** - An array of [`submatch` objects](#object-submatch)
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:266:///   corresponding to matches in `lines`. The offsets included in each
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:267:///   `submatch` correspond to byte offsets into `lines`. (If `lines` is base64
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:268:///   encoded, then the byte offsets correspond to the data after base64
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:269:///   decoding.) The `submatch` objects are guaranteed to be sorted by their
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:270:///   starting offsets. Note that it is possible for this array to be empty,
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:271:///   for example, when searching reports inverted matches. If the configuration
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:272:///   specifies a replacement, the resulting replacement text is also present.
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:273:///
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:274:/// #### Message: **context**
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:275:///
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:276:/// This message indicates that a contextual line has been found. A contextual
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:277:/// line is a line that doesn't contain a match, but is generally adjacent to
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:278:/// a line that does contain a match. The precise way in which contextual lines
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:279:/// are reported is determined by the searcher. It has these fields, which are
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:280:/// exactly the same fields found in a [`match`](#message-match):
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:281:///
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:282:/// * **path** - An
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:283:///   [arbitrary data object](#object-arbitrary-data)
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:284:///   representing the file path corresponding to the search, if one is
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:285:///   present. If no file path is available, then this field is `null`.
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:286:/// * **lines** - An
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:287:///   [arbitrary data object](#object-arbitrary-data)
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:288:///   representing one or more lines contained in this context. This includes
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:289:///   line terminators, if they're present.
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:290:/// * **line_number** - If the searcher has been configured to report line
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:291:///   numbers, then this corresponds to the line number of the first line
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:292:///   in `lines`. If no line numbers are available, then this is `null`.
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:293:/// * **absolute_offset** - The absolute byte offset corresponding to the start
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:294:///   of `lines` in the data being searched.
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:295:/// * **submatches** - An array of [`submatch` objects](#object-submatch)
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:296:///   corresponding to matches in `lines`. The offsets included in each
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:297:///   `submatch` correspond to byte offsets into `lines`. (If `lines` is base64
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:298:///   encoded, then the byte offsets correspond to the data after base64
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:299:///   decoding.) The `submatch` objects are guaranteed to be sorted by
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:300:///   their starting offsets. Note that it is possible for this array to be
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:301:///   non-empty, for example, when searching reports inverted matches such that
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:302:///   the original matcher could match things in the contextual lines. If the
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:303:///   configuration specifies a replacemement, the resulting replacement text
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:304:///   is also present.
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:305:///
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:306:/// #### Object: **submatch**
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:307:///
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:308:/// This object describes submatches found within `match` or `context`
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:309:/// messages. The `start` and `end` fields indicate the half-open interval on
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:310:/// which the match occurs (`start` is included, but `end` is not). It is
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:311:/// guaranteed that `start <= end`. It has these fields:
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:312:///
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:313:/// * **match** - An
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:314:///   [arbitrary data object](#object-arbitrary-data)
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:315:///   corresponding to the text in this submatch.
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:316:/// * **start** - A byte offset indicating the start of this match. This offset
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:317:///   is generally reported in terms of the parent object's data. For example,
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:318:///   the `lines` field in the
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:319:///   [`match`](#message-match) or [`context`](#message-context)
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:320:///   messages.
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:321:/// * **end** - A byte offset indicating the end of this match. This offset
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:322:///   is generally reported in terms of the parent object's data. For example,
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:323:///   the `lines` field in the
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:324:///   [`match`](#message-match) or [`context`](#message-context)
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:325:///   messages.
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:326:/// * **replacement** (optional) - An
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:327:///   [arbitrary data object](#object-arbitrary-data) corresponding to the
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:328:///   replacement text for this submatch, if the configuration specifies
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:329:///   a replacement.
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:330:///
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:331:/// #### Object: **stats**
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:332:///
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:333:/// This object is included in messages and contains summary statistics about
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:334:/// a search. It has these fields:
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:335:///
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:336:/// * **elapsed** - A [`duration` object](#object-duration) describing the
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:337:///   length of time that elapsed while performing the search.
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:338:/// * **searches** - The number of searches that have run. For this printer,
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:339:///   this value is always `1`. (Implementations may emit additional message
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:340:///   types that use this same `stats` object that represents summary
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:341:///   statistics over multiple searches.)
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:342:/// * **searches_with_match** - The number of searches that have run that have
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:343:///   found at least one match. This is never more than `searches`.
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:344:/// * **bytes_searched** - The total number of bytes that have been searched.
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:345:/// * **bytes_printed** - The total number of bytes that have been printed.
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:346:///   This includes everything emitted by this printer.
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:347:/// * **matched_lines** - The total number of lines that participated in a
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:348:///   match. When matches may contain multiple lines, then this includes every
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:349:///   line that is part of every match.
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:350:/// * **matches** - The total number of matches. There may be multiple matches
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:351:///   per line. When matches may contain multiple lines, each match is counted
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:352:///   only once, regardless of how many lines it spans.
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:353:///
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:354:/// #### Object: **duration**
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:355:///
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:356:/// This object includes a few fields for describing a duration. Two of its
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:357:/// fields, `secs` and `nanos`, can be combined to give nanosecond precision
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:358:/// on systems that support it. It has these fields:
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:359:///
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:360:/// * **secs** - A whole number of seconds indicating the length of this
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:361:///   duration.
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:362:/// * **nanos** - A fractional part of this duration represent by nanoseconds.
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:363:///   If nanosecond precision isn't supported, then this is typically rounded
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:364:///   up to the nearest number of nanoseconds.
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:365:/// * **human** - A human readable string describing the length of the
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:366:///   duration. The format of the string is itself unspecified.
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:367:///
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:368:/// #### Object: **arbitrary data**
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:369:///
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:370:/// This object is used whenever arbitrary data needs to be represented as a
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:371:/// JSON value. This object contains two fields, where generally only one of
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:372:/// the fields is present:
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:373:///
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:374:/// * **text** - A normal JSON string that is UTF-8 encoded. This field is
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:375:///   populated if and only if the underlying data is valid UTF-8.
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:376:/// * **bytes** - A normal JSON string that is a base64 encoding of the
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:377:///   underlying bytes.
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:378:///
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:379:/// More information on the motivation for this representation can be seen in
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:380:/// the section [text encoding](#text-encoding) above.
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:381:///
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:382:/// ## Example
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:383:///
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:384:/// This section shows a small example that includes all message types.
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:385:///
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:386:/// Here's the file we want to search, located at `/home/andrew/sherlock`:
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:387:///
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:388:/// ```text
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:389:/// For the Doctor Watsons of this world, as opposed to the Sherlock
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:390:/// Holmeses, success in the province of detective work must always
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:391:/// be, to a very large extent, the result of luck. Sherlock Holmes
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:392:/// can extract a clew from a wisp of straw or a flake of cigar ash;
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:393:/// but Doctor Watson has to have it taken out for him and dusted,
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:394:/// and exhibited clearly, with a label attached.
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:395:/// ```
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:396:///
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:397:/// Searching for `Watson` with a `before_context` of `1` with line numbers
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:398:/// enabled shows something like this using the standard printer:
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:399:///
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:400:/// ```text
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:401:/// sherlock:1:For the Doctor Watsons of this world, as opposed to the Sherlock
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:402:/// --
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:403:/// sherlock-4-can extract a clew from a wisp of straw or a flake of cigar ash;
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:404:/// sherlock:5:but Doctor Watson has to have it taken out for him and dusted,
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:405:/// ```
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:406:///
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:407:/// Here's what the same search looks like using the JSON wire format described
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:408:/// above, where in we show semi-prettified JSON (instead of a strict JSON
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:409:/// Lines format), for illustrative purposes:
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:410:///
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:411:/// ```json
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:412:/// {
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:413:///   "type": "begin",
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:414:///   "data": {
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:415:///     "path": {"text": "/home/andrew/sherlock"}}
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:416:///   }
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:417:/// }
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:418:/// {
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:419:///   "type": "match",
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:420:///   "data": {
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:421:///     "path": {"text": "/home/andrew/sherlock"},
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:422:///     "lines": {"text": "For the Doctor Watsons of this world, as opposed to the Sherlock\n"},
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:423:///     "line_number": 1,
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:424:///     "absolute_offset": 0,
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:425:///     "submatches": [
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:426:///       {"match": {"text": "Watson"}, "start": 15, "end": 21}
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:427:///     ]
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:428:///   }
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:429:/// }
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:430:/// {
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:431:///   "type": "context",
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:432:///   "data": {
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:433:///     "path": {"text": "/home/andrew/sherlock"},
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:434:///     "lines": {"text": "can extract a clew from a wisp of straw or a flake of cigar ash;\n"},
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:435:///     "line_number": 4,
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:436:///     "absolute_offset": 193,
./crates/printer/src/json.rs:437:///     "submatches": []

./crates/globset/README.md:3:Cross platform single glob and glob set matching. Glob set matching is the
./crates/globset/README.md:4:process of matching one or more glob patterns against a single candidate path
./crates/globset/README.md:5:simultaneously, and returning all of the globs that matched.

./crates/globset/README.md:12:### Documentation

./crates/globset/README.md:14:[https://docs.rs/globset](https://docs.rs/globset)
./crates/globset/README.md:15:
./crates/globset/README.md:16:### Usage
./crates/globset/README.md:17:
./crates/globset/README.md:18:Add this to your `Cargo.toml`:

./crates/globset/README.md:20:```toml
./crates/globset/README.md:21:[dependencies]
./crates/globset/README.md:22:globset = "0.4"
./crates/globset/README.md:23:```
./crates/globset/README.md:24:
./crates/globset/README.md:25:### Features
./crates/globset/README.md:26:
./crates/globset/README.md:27:* `serde1`: Enables implementing Serde traits on the `Glob` type.
./crates/globset/README.md:28:
./crates/globset/README.md:29:### Example: one glob
./crates/globset/README.md:30:
./crates/globset/README.md:31:This example shows how to match a single glob against a single file path.
./crates/globset/README.md:32:
./crates/globset/README.md:33:```rust
./crates/globset/README.md:34:use globset::Glob;
./crates/globset/README.md:35:
./crates/globset/README.md:36:let glob = Glob::new("*.rs")?.compile_matcher();
./crates/globset/README.md:37:
./crates/globset/README.md:38:assert!(glob.is_match("foo.rs"));
./crates/globset/README.md:39:assert!(glob.is_match("foo/bar.rs"));
./crates/globset/README.md:40:assert!(!glob.is_match("Cargo.toml"));
./crates/globset/README.md:41:```
./crates/globset/README.md:42:
./crates/globset/README.md:43:### Example: configuring a glob matcher
./crates/globset/README.md:44:
./crates/globset/README.md:45:This example shows how to use a `GlobBuilder` to configure aspects of match
./crates/globset/README.md:46:semantics. In this example, we prevent wildcards from matching path separators.
./crates/globset/README.md:47:
./crates/globset/README.md:48:```rust
./crates/globset/README.md:49:use globset::GlobBuilder;
./crates/globset/README.md:50:
./crates/globset/README.md:51:let glob = GlobBuilder::new("*.rs")
./crates/globset/README.md:52:    .literal_separator(true).build()?.compile_matcher();
./crates/globset/README.md:53:
./crates/globset/README.md:54:assert!(glob.is_match("foo.rs"));
./crates/globset/README.md:55:assert!(!glob.is_match("foo/bar.rs")); // no longer matches
./crates/globset/README.md:56:assert!(!glob.is_match("Cargo.toml"));
./crates/globset/README.md:57:```
./crates/globset/README.md:58:
./crates/globset/README.md:59:### Example: match multiple globs at once
./crates/globset/README.md:60:
./crates/globset/README.md:61:This example shows how to match multiple glob patterns at once.
./crates/globset/README.md:62:
./crates/globset/README.md:63:```rust
./crates/globset/README.md:64:use globset::{Glob, GlobSetBuilder};
./crates/globset/README.md:65:
./crates/globset/README.md:66:let mut builder = GlobSetBuilder::new();
./crates/globset/README.md:67:// A GlobBuilder can be used to configure each glob's match semantics
./crates/globset/README.md:68:// independently.
./crates/globset/README.md:69:builder.add(Glob::new("*.rs")?);
./crates/globset/README.md:70:builder.add(Glob::new("src/lib.rs")?);
./crates/globset/README.md:71:builder.add(Glob::new("src/**/foo.rs")?);
./crates/globset/README.md:72:let set = builder.build()?;
./crates/globset/README.md:73:
./crates/globset/README.md:74:assert_eq!(set.matches("src/bar/baz/foo.rs"), vec![0, 2]);
./crates/globset/README.md:75:```
./crates/globset/README.md:76:
./crates/globset/README.md:77:### Performance
./crates/globset/README.md:78:
./crates/globset/README.md:79:This crate implements globs by converting them to regular expressions, and
./crates/globset/README.md:80:executing them with the
./crates/globset/README.md:81:[`regex`](https://github.com/rust-lang/regex)
./crates/globset/README.md:82:crate.
./crates/globset/README.md:83:
./crates/globset/README.md:84:For single glob matching, performance of this crate should be roughly on par
./crates/globset/README.md:85:with the performance of the
./crates/globset/README.md:86:[`glob`](https://github.com/rust-lang/glob)
./crates/globset/README.md:87:crate. (`*_regex` correspond to benchmarks for this library while `*_glob`
./crates/globset/README.md:88:correspond to benchmarks for the `glob` library.)
./crates/globset/README.md:89:Optimizations in the `regex` crate may propel this library past `glob`,
./crates/globset/README.md:90:particularly when matching longer paths.
./crates/globset/README.md:91:
./crates/globset/README.md:92:```
./crates/globset/README.md:93:test ext_glob             ... bench:         425 ns/iter (+/- 21)
./crates/globset/README.md:94:test ext_regex            ... bench:         175 ns/iter (+/- 10)
./crates/globset/README.md:95:test long_glob            ... bench:         182 ns/iter (+/- 11)
./crates/globset/README.md:96:test long_regex           ... bench:         173 ns/iter (+/- 10)
./crates/globset/README.md:97:test short_glob           ... bench:          69 ns/iter (+/- 4)
./crates/globset/README.md:98:test short_regex          ... bench:          83 ns/iter (+/- 2)
./crates/globset/README.md:99:```
./crates/globset/README.md:100:
./crates/globset/README.md:101:The primary performance advantage of this crate is when matching multiple
./crates/globset/README.md:102:globs against a single path. With the `glob` crate, one must match each glob
./crates/globset/README.md:103:synchronously, one after the other. In this crate, many can be matched
./crates/globset/README.md:104:simultaneously. For example:
./crates/globset/README.md:105:
./crates/globset/README.md:106:```
./crates/globset/README.md:107:test many_short_glob      ... bench:       1,063 ns/iter (+/- 47)
./crates/globset/README.md:108:test many_short_regex_set ... bench:         186 ns/iter (+/- 11)
./crates/globset/README.md:109:```
./crates/globset/README.md:110:
./crates/globset/README.md:111:### Comparison with the [`glob`](https://github.com/rust-lang/glob) crate
./crates/globset/README.md:112:
./crates/globset/README.md:113:* Supports alternate "or" globs, e.g., `*.{foo,bar}`.
./crates/globset/README.md:114:* Can match non-UTF-8 file paths correctly.
./crates/globset/README.md:115:* Supports matching multiple globs at once.
./crates/globset/README.md:116:* Doesn't provide a recursive directory iterator of matching file paths,
./crates/globset/README.md:117:  although I believe this crate should grow one eventually.
./crates/globset/README.md:118:* Supports case insensitive and require-literal-separator match options, but
./crates/globset/README.md:119:  **doesn't** support the require-literal-leading-dot option.

        self,
        request: Request,
        auth: Auth,
        follow_redirects: bool,
        history: list[Response],
    ) -> Response:
        auth_flow = auth.async_auth_flow(request)
        try:
            request = await auth_flow.__anext__()

            while True:
                response = await self._send_handling_redirects(
                    request,
                    follow_redirects=follow_redirects,
                    history=history,
                )
                try:
                    try:
                        next_request = await auth_flow.asend(response)
                    except StopAsyncIteration:
                        return response

                    response.history = list(history)
                    await response.aread()
                    request = next_request
                    history.append(response)

                except BaseException as exc:
                    await response.aclose()
                    raise exc
        finally:

    async def send(
        self,
        request: Request,
        *,
        stream: bool = False,
        auth: AuthTypes | UseClientDefault | None = USE_CLIENT_DEFAULT,
        follow_redirects: bool | UseClientDefault = USE_CLIENT_DEFAULT,
    ) -> Response:
        """
        Send a request.

        The request is sent as-is, unmodified.

        Typically you'll want to build one with `AsyncClient.build_request()`
        so that any client-level configuration is merged into the request,
        but passing an explicit `httpx.Request()` is supported as well.

        See also: [Request instances][0]

        [0]: /advanced/clients/#request-instances
        """
        if self._state == ClientState.CLOSED:
            raise RuntimeError("Cannot send a request, as the client has been closed.")

        self._state = ClientState.OPENED
        follow_redirects = (
            self.follow_redirects
            if isinstance(follow_redirects, UseClientDefault)
            else follow_redirects
        )

        self._set_timeout(request)

        auth = self._build_request_auth(request, auth)

        response = await self._send_handling_auth(
            request,
            auth=auth,
            follow_redirects=follow_redirects,
            history=[],
        )
        try:
            if not stream:
                await response.aread()

            return response

        except BaseException as exc:
            await response.aclose()
            raise exc

    async def _send_handling_auth(
        self,
        request: Request,
        auth: Auth,
        follow_redirects: bool,
        history: list[Response],
    ) -> Response:
        auth_flow = auth.async_auth_flow(request)
        try:
            request = await auth_flow.__anext__()

            while True:
                response = await self._send_handling_redirects(
                    request,
                    follow_redirects=follow_redirects,
                    history=history,
                )
                try:
                    try:
                        next_request = await auth_flow.asend(response)
                    except StopAsyncIteration:
                        return response

                    response.history = list(history)
                    await response.aread()
                    request = next_request
                    history.append(response)

                except BaseException as exc:
                    await response.aclose()
                    raise exc
        finally:
            await auth_flow.aclose()

    async def _send_handling_redirects(
        self,
        request: Request,
        follow_redirects: bool,
        history: list[Response],
    ) -> Response:
        while True:
            if len(history) > self.max_redirects:
                raise TooManyRedirects(
                    "Exceeded maximum allowed redirects.", request=request
                )

class Auth:

    Base class for all authentication schemes.

    To implement a custom authentication scheme, subclass `Auth` and override
    the `.auth_flow()` method.

    If the authentication scheme does I/O such as disk access or network calls, or uses
    synchronization primitives such as locks, you should override `.sync_auth_flow()`
    and/or `.async_auth_flow()` instead of `.auth_flow()` to provide specialized
    implementations that will be used by `Client` and `AsyncClient` respectively.
    """

    requires_request_body = False
    requires_response_body = False

    def auth_flow(self, request: Request) -> typing.Generator[Request, Response, None]:
        """
        Execute the authentication flow.

        To dispatch a request, `yield` it:

        ```
        yield request
        ```

        The client will `.send()` the response back into the flow generator. You can
        access it like so:

        ```
        response = yield request
        ```

        A `return` (or reaching the end of the generator) will result in the
        client returning the last response obtained from the server.

        You can dispatch as many requests as is necessary.
        """
        yield request

    def sync_auth_flow(
        self, request: Request
    ) -> typing.Generator[Request, Response, None]:
        """
        Execute the authentication flow synchronously.

        By default, this defers to `.auth_flow()`. You should override this method
        when the authentication scheme does I/O and/or uses concurrency primitives.
        """
        if self.requires_request_body:
            request.read()

        flow = self.auth_flow(request)
        request = next(flow)

        while True:
            response = yield request
            if self.requires_response_body:

            try:

            except StopIteration:

    async def async_auth_flow(
        self, request: Request

class LineDecoder:
    """
    Handles incrementally reading lines from text.

    Has the same behaviour as the stdllib splitlines,
    but handling the input iteratively.
    """

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.buffer: list[str] = []
        self.trailing_cr: bool = False

    def decode(self, text: str) -> list[str]:
        # See https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str.splitlines
        NEWLINE_CHARS = "\n\r\x0b\x0c\x1c\x1d\x1e\x85\u2028\u2029"

        # We always push a trailing `\r` into the next decode iteration.
        if self.trailing_cr:
            text = "\r" + text
            self.trailing_cr = False
        if text.endswith("\r"):
            self.trailing_cr = True
            text = text[:-1]

        if not text:
            # NOTE: the edge case input of empty text doesn't occur in practice,
            # because other httpx internals filter out this value
            return []  # pragma: no cover

        trailing_newline = text[-1] in NEWLINE_CHARS
        lines = text.splitlines()

        if len(lines) == 1 and not trailing_newline:
            # No new lines, buffer the input and continue.
            self.buffer.append(lines[0])
            return []

        if self.buffer:
            # Include any existing buffer in the first portion of the
            # splitlines result.
            lines = ["".join(self.buffer) + lines[0]] + lines[1:]
            self.buffer = []

        if not trailing_newline:
            # If the last segment of splitlines is not newline terminated,
            # then drop it from our output and start a new buffer.
            self.buffer = [lines.pop()]

        return lines

    def flush(self) -> list[str]:
        if not self.buffer and not self.trailing_cr:
            return []

        lines = ["".join(self.buffer)]
        self.buffer = []
        self.trailing_cr = False
        return lines

def auth_flow(
        self, request: httpx.Request
    ) -> typing.Generator[httpx.Request, httpx.Response, None]:
        nonces = []

        for index in range(self.repeat):
            request.headers["Authorization"] = f"Repeat {index}"
            response = yield request
            nonces.append(response.headers["www-authenticate"])

        key = ".".join(nonces)
        request.headers["Authorization"] = f"Repeat {key}"
        yield request


class ResponseBodyAuth(httpx.Auth):
    """
    A mock authentication scheme that requires clients to send an 'Authorization'
    header, then send back the contents of the response in the 'Authorization'
    header.
    """

    requires_response_body = True

    def __init__(self, token: str) -> None:
        self.token = token

    def auth_flow(
        self, request: httpx.Request
    ) -> typing.Generator[httpx.Request, httpx.Response, None]:
        request.headers["Authorization"] = self.token
        response = yield request
        data = response.text
        request.headers["Authorization"] = data

    """

./fuzz/README.md:1:# Fuzz Testing
./fuzz/README.md:2:
./fuzz/README.md:3:## Introduction
./fuzz/README.md:4:
./fuzz/README.md:5:Fuzz testing produces pseudo-random / arbitrary data that is used to find
./fuzz/README.md:6:stability issues within a code base. While Rust provides a strong type system,
./fuzz/README.md:7:this does not guarantee that an object will convert properly from one struct
./fuzz/README.md:8:to another. It is the responsibility of the developer to ensure that a struct
./fuzz/README.md:9:is converted properly. Fuzz testing will generate input within the domain of
./fuzz/README.md:10:each property. This arbitrary data can then be used to convert from ObjectA
./fuzz/README.md:11:to ObjectB and then back. This type of testing will help catch bugs that the
./fuzz/README.md:12:type system is not able to see.
./fuzz/README.md:13:
./fuzz/README.md:14:## Installation
./fuzz/README.md:15:
./fuzz/README.md:16:This crate relies on the `cargo-fuzz` component. To install this component,
./fuzz/README.md:17:run the following from the `fuzz` directory:
./fuzz/README.md:18:
./fuzz/README.md:19:```bash
./fuzz/README.md:20:cargo install cargo-fuzz
./fuzz/README.md:21:```
./fuzz/README.md:22:
./fuzz/README.md:23:## Listing Targets
./fuzz/README.md:24:
./fuzz/README.md:25:Once installed, fuzz targets can be listed by running the following command:
./fuzz/README.md:26:
./fuzz/README.md:27:```bash
./fuzz/README.md:28:cargo fuzz list
./fuzz/README.md:29:```
./fuzz/README.md:30:
./fuzz/README.md:31:This command will print out a list of all targets that can be tested.
./fuzz/README.md:32:
./fuzz/README.md:33:## Running Fuzz Tests
./fuzz/README.md:34:
./fuzz/README.md:35:To run a fuzz test, the target must be specified:
./fuzz/README.md:36:
./fuzz/README.md:37:```bash
./fuzz/README.md:38:cargo fuzz run <target>
./fuzz/README.md:39:```
./fuzz/README.md:40:
./fuzz/README.md:41:Note that the above will run the fuzz test indefinitely. Use the
./fuzz/README.md:42:`-max_total_time=<num seconds>` flag to specify how many seconds the test
./fuzz/README.md:43:should run for:
./fuzz/README.md:44:
./fuzz/README.md:45:```bash
./fuzz/README.md:46:cargo fuzz run <target> -- -max_total_time=5
./fuzz/README.md:47:```
./fuzz/README.md:48:
./fuzz/README.md:49:The above command will run the fuzz test for five seconds. If the test
./fuzz/README.md:50:completes without error it will show how many tests were run successfully.
./fuzz/README.md:51:The test will abort and return a non-zero error code if it is able to produce
./fuzz/README.md:52:an error. The arbitrary input will be displayed in the event of a failure.

./RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md:1:# Release Checklist
./RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md:2:
./RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md:3:* Ensure local `master` is up to date with respect to `origin/master`.
./RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md:4:* Run `cargo update` and review dependency updates. Commit updated
./RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md:5:  `Cargo.lock`.
./RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md:6:* Run `cargo outdated` and review semver incompatible updates. Unless there is
./RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md:7:  a strong motivation otherwise, review and update every dependency. Also
./RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md:8:  run `--aggressive`, but don't update to crates that are still in beta.
./RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md:9:* Update date in `crates/core/flags/doc/template.rg.1`.
./RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md:10:* Update the CHANGELOG as appropriate.
./RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md:11:* Review changes for every crate in `crates` since the last ripgrep release.
./RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md:12:  If the set of changes is non-empty, issue a new release for that crate. Check
./RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md:13:  crates in the following order. After updating a crate, ensure minimal
./RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md:14:  versions are updated as appropriate in dependents. If an update is required,
./RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md:15:  run `cargo-up --no-push crates/{CRATE}/Cargo.toml`.
./RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md:16:    * crates/globset
./RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md:17:    * crates/ignore
./RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md:18:    * crates/cli
./RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md:19:    * crates/matcher
./RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md:20:    * crates/regex
./RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md:21:    * crates/pcre2
./RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md:22:    * crates/searcher
./RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md:23:    * crates/printer
./RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md:24:    * crates/grep (bump minimal versions as necessary)
./RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md:25:    * crates/core (do **not** bump version, but update dependencies as needed)
./RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md:26:* Edit the `Cargo.toml` to set the new ripgrep version. Run
./RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md:27:  `cargo update -p ripgrep` so that the `Cargo.lock` is updated. Commit the
./RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md:28:  changes and create a new signed tag. Alternatively, use
./RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md:29:  `cargo-up --no-push --no-release Cargo.toml {VERSION}` to automate this.
./RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md:30:* Run `cargo package` and ensure it succeeds.
./RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md:31:* Push changes to GitHub, NOT including the tag. (But do not publish a new
./RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md:32:  version of ripgrep to crates.io yet.)
./RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md:33:* Once CI for `master` finishes successfully, push the version tag. (Trying to
./RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md:34:  do this in one step seems to result in GitHub Actions not seeing the tag
./RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md:35:  push and thus not running the release workflow.)
./RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md:36:* Wait for CI to finish creating the release. If the release build fails, then
./RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md:37:  delete the tag from GitHub, make fixes, re-tag, delete the release and push.
./RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md:38:* Copy the relevant section of the CHANGELOG to the tagged release notes.
./RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md:39:  Include this blurb describing what ripgrep is:
./RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md:40:  > In case you haven't heard of it before, ripgrep is a line-oriented search
./RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md:41:  > tool that recursively searches the current directory for a regex pattern.
./RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md:42:  > By default, ripgrep will respect gitignore rules and automatically skip
./RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md:43:  > hidden files/directories and binary files.
./RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md:44:* Run `cargo publish`.
./RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md:45:* Run `ci/sha256-releases {VERSION} >> pkg/brew/ripgrep-bin.rb`. Then edit
./RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md:46:  `pkg/brew/ripgrep-bin.rb` to update the version number and sha256 hashes.
./RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md:47:  Remove extraneous stuff added by `ci/sha256-releases`. Commit changes.
./RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md:48:* Add TBD section to the top of the CHANGELOG:
./RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md:49:  ```
./RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md:50:  TBD
./RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md:51:  ===
./RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md:52:  Unreleased changes. Release notes have not yet been written.
./RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md:53:  ```
./RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md:54:
./RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md:55:Note that [`cargo-up` can be found in BurntSushi's dotfiles][dotfiles].
./RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md:56:
./RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md:57:[dotfiles]: https://github.com/BurntSushi/dotfiles/blob/master/bin/cargo-up

./.github/workflows/ci.yml:10:# The section is needed to drop write-all permissions that are granted on
./.github/workflows/ci.yml:11:# `schedule` event. By specifying any permission explicitly all others are set
./.github/workflows/ci.yml:12:# to none. By using the principle of least privilege the damage a compromised
./.github/workflows/ci.yml:13:# workflow can do (because of an injection or compromised third party tool or
./.github/workflows/ci.yml:14:# action) is restricted. Currently the workflow doesn't need any additional
./.github/workflows/ci.yml:15:# permission except for pulling the code. Adding labels to issues, commenting
./.github/workflows/ci.yml:16:# on pull-requests, etc. may need additional permissions:
./.github/workflows/ci.yml:17:#
./.github/workflows/ci.yml:18:# Syntax for this section:
./.github/workflows/ci.yml:19:# https://docs.github.com/en/actions/using-workflows/workflow-syntax-for-github-actions#permissions
./.github/workflows/ci.yml:20:#
./.github/workflows/ci.yml:21:# Reference for how to assign permissions on a job-by-job basis:
./.github/workflows/ci.yml:22:# https://docs.github.com/en/actions/using-jobs/assigning-permissions-to-jobs
./.github/workflows/ci.yml:23:#
./.github/workflows/ci.yml:24:# Reference for available permissions that we can enable if needed:
./.github/workflows/ci.yml:25:# https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-guides/automatic-token-authentication#permissions-for-the-github_token
./.github/workflows/ci.yml:26:permissions:

./.github/workflows/ci.yml:28:  contents: read

./.github/workflows/ci.yml:33:    env:
./.github/workflows/ci.yml:34:      # For some builds, we use cross to test on 32-bit and big-endian
./.github/workflows/ci.yml:35:      # systems.
./.github/workflows/ci.yml:36:      CARGO: cargo
./.github/workflows/ci.yml:37:      # When CARGO is set to CROSS, this is set to `--target matrix.target`.
./.github/workflows/ci.yml:38:      # Note that we only use cross on Linux, so setting a target on a
./.github/workflows/ci.yml:39:      # different OS will just use normal cargo.
./.github/workflows/ci.yml:40:      TARGET_FLAGS:
./.github/workflows/ci.yml:41:      # When CARGO is set to CROSS, TARGET_DIR includes matrix.target.
./.github/workflows/ci.yml:42:      TARGET_DIR: ./target
./.github/workflows/ci.yml:43:      # Bump this as appropriate. We pin to a version to make sure CI
./.github/workflows/ci.yml:44:      # continues to work as cross releases in the past have broken things
./.github/workflows/ci.yml:45:      # in subtle ways.
./.github/workflows/ci.yml:46:      CROSS_VERSION: v0.2.5
./.github/workflows/ci.yml:47:      # Emit backtraces on panics.
./.github/workflows/ci.yml:48:      RUST_BACKTRACE: 1

./AI_POLICY.md:1:# AI Policy
./AI_POLICY.md:2:
./AI_POLICY.md:3:Using AI (i.e., LLMs) as tools for coding is welcome. A high bar is held for
./AI_POLICY.md:4:all contributions to this project. Moreover, the project maintainers remain
./AI_POLICY.md:5:responsible for any code that is published as part of a release. Contributors
./AI_POLICY.md:6:are expected to be responsible for any code they publish.
./AI_POLICY.md:7:
./AI_POLICY.md:8:**AI should not be used to generate comments when communicating with
./AI_POLICY.md:9:maintainers**. Comments are expected to be written by humans. Comments that are
./AI_POLICY.md:10:believed to be written by AI may be hidden without notice.
./AI_POLICY.md:11:
./AI_POLICY.md:12:If you are opening an issue, you should be able to describe the problem in your
./AI_POLICY.md:13:own words.
./AI_POLICY.md:14:
./AI_POLICY.md:15:If you are opening a pull request, you are expected to be able to explain the
./AI_POLICY.md:16:proposed changes in your own words. This includes the pull request body and
./AI_POLICY.md:17:responses to questions. **Do not copy responses from the AI when replying to
./AI_POLICY.md:18:questions from maintainers.**
./AI_POLICY.md:19:
./AI_POLICY.md:20:This project requires a human in the loop who understands the work produced by
./AI_POLICY.md:21:AI. **Autonomous agents are not allowed to be used for contributing to this
./AI_POLICY.md:22:project**. Pull requests that appear in violation of this will be closed,
./AI_POLICY.md:23:perhaps without notice.
./AI_POLICY.md:24:
./AI_POLICY.md:25:If you wish to include context from an interaction with AI in your comments, it
./AI_POLICY.md:26:must be in a quote block (e.g., using `>`) and disclosed as such. It must be
./AI_POLICY.md:27:accompanied by human commentary explaining the relevance and implications of
./AI_POLICY.md:28:the context. Do not share long snippets.
./AI_POLICY.md:29:
./AI_POLICY.md:30:AI is useful when communicating as a non-native English speaker. If you are
./AI_POLICY.md:31:using AI to edit your comments for this purpose, please take the time to ensure
./AI_POLICY.md:32:it reflects your own voice and ideas. If using AI for translation, we recommend
./AI_POLICY.md:33:writing in your native language and including the AI translation in a quote
./AI_POLICY.md:34:block.
./AI_POLICY.md:35:
./AI_POLICY.md:36:This policy was adapted from [uv's AI policy].
./AI_POLICY.md:37:
./AI_POLICY.md:38:[uv's AI policy]: https://github.com/astral-sh/.github/blob/c5187e200db51bfe11d56e13053d29bd3793fdd8/AI_POLICY.md
